_doc: Character system (드라마 등장인물): the rig's geometry in local units and every staging's shots in screen px. One source of truth for video/src/rig.ts, Body.tsx, Character.tsx, Animal.tsx, CastScene.tsx and tests/test_characters.py, which checks the composition rules: eyes in the eye band, faces and hands never in the caption band / bottom 20% / right UI column (unless a foreground prop hides them), shot sizes, the body-length rule, at most 3 characters per shot. Local rig units: origin at the base of the neck, y down; a character drawn with scale k at (x, eyeY) has its neck at (x, eyeY - rig.eyeY * k).
_characters: ad = the voice of an on-screen ad (watch_ad): drawn as a generic invented presenter inside the TV frame, never a real person
_castStyles: A skin over the same rig and stagings (script field cast_style, default human): human = Character.tsx, animal = Animal.tsx (진돗개 family: father white, mother tan with a perm; 여우 callers: scammer in a hoodie and headset, fake_banker a silver-grey fox in a suit with a blank badge, ad presenter in a shiny suit). Both skins share the body (Body.tsx, 'bodies'). The animal head keeps to the rig's head box: ear tips no higher than rig.head.top, half width (with cheek fur) within rig.head.rx + 34, the jowl/chin no lower than rig.head.chin; eyes and mouth on rig.eyeY / rig.mouthY.
_animal: eye: the white of an animal eye in local units (height 2*ry = 17% of the head height); shockedMouth: half width of the shocked mouth (2x = 30-40% of faceWidth), with teeth and tongue
_outlinePx: the ink outline in screen px, the same at every shot size: the rig's stroke widths are divided by the character's on-screen scale

rig._hands: hand centres per gesture and side (L = viewer's left, R = viewer's right); a side a gesture leaves free hangs at rest (paw at the hip)

_bodies: SD body per character (local units, half widths; head height H = 382, head width 320): sh shoulders, w the torso's widest, waistY/waistW the waist, hemY the top's hem, hip, crotch, sole (the feet's bottom), legX/legW the legs' centre and half width, skirt (bottom y, half width). Chin->waist 0.6-0.75 H, torso 1.05-1.2 x the head width, parents ~2.7 heads tall, the children ~2.9, the fox callers ~3.0 (lankier = more threatening).
_shotSizes: head height (hair line to chin) as a share of the 1920 frame height, per shot size. The body-length rule (tests): without visible feet, the body below the chin down to bodyRule.line (or a foreground prop's top) is at most bodyRule.maxBelowChin heads; a 'full' shot shows the feet above that line instead.
_props: foreground props drawn in front of the characters (Sets.tsx ForegroundProp): table = the home's table edge (living room, sofa corner), desk = the office desk (work), ccDesk = the call centre's desk. top = the prop's top edge in screen px; it hides the body and the resting paws below it.
_shots: Per staging, the shots it cuts between. A character entry: who (victim | caller | other | presenter), x (neck x), eyeY, k (scale), turn (-1..1, face turned to the viewer's left/right), gestures used in that shot (for the hand checks; the performance may vary it among those listed in gestures), view (front | back). size: the shot size (shotSizes); prop: the foreground prop; windows: framed insets in screen px.

pip_call._hook: the opening shot (the poster and thumbnail): the victim's extreme close-up with the phone at the ear; the caller's window springs in on the first cut

split_call._split: the caller's panel is the top part (y 236 to the border), the victim's the bottom (border to 1250); the border is tilted 3 degrees

over_shoulder_chat._over: back view: the eye line stands for the back of the head (no face); the phone glows in the hand and the mockup panel floats above it

_motion: cheap motion, all pure functions of the frame: a punch-in on the scene's keyword (the line's bubble, else the scene's mark when a line says it), a camera shake as a shocked/panicked line starts, a 4-frame squash when a face changes
